stage: Exploratory fixed computational-control plan following explicit AI-pretest source clarification; not preregistration or untouched validation
question: Can the cross-task pairing of the fixed AI pretest batch change panel heterogeneity and human-target predictive scores while every training task-by-version choice count remains exactly fixed?
units: Original human records and fixed AI-pretest records. Derived re-pairings are computational controls, never newly observed responses.
training_and_target: Use the existing five record folds. In each fold keep human training records, held-out human records, menus and the original training AI counts fixed. Re-pair only training AI answers within version, independently by task. Score only original held-out human records.
outcomes: human-heldout joint and marginal log scores
exact_control: Verify each task-by-version count and the MNL objective/gradient at its fitted parameters. Re-pairing preserves the ordinary MNL objective exactly; this established invariance is a control, not a new theorem.
interpretation: Effects are of an explicit data operation on this fixed batch. They do not identify population-level human-versus-AI causal differences, generator mechanisms or platform-wide prevalence.
uncertainty: Ten fixed re-pairings are a procedural sensitivity analysis, not a permutation p-value, power simulation or ten independent AI-generation batches.
stopping_rule: Run the stated models and seeds; retain all outcomes. No new models or seed selection based on observed gains.
